images.caption: The Old Pier at Weston-super-Mare, Somerset, England. This was used by steam ships sailing on the Bristol Channel and many amusements were installed on the pier so that visitors would spend their mioney their rather than travel further into the town. The building on the left is the lifeboat station.

images.filename: 2011 at Birnbeck Pier - temporary lifeboat house.jpg
images.caption: Birnbeck Island, Weston-super-Mare, Somerset. The town's three lifeboat stations can be seen: the white building is the current "temporary" structure which was erected in April 2011; next to the pier on the right is the first boathouse which was used from 1889 until 1902; on the left with the long slipway is the 1902 building.
images.alt: Birnbeck Island, Weston-super-Mare, Somerset. The town's three lifeboat stations can be seen: the white building is the current "temporary" structure which was erected in April 2011; next to the pier on the right is the first boathouse which was used from 1889 until 1902; on the left with the long slipway is the 1902 building.

images.caption: The old Birnbeck Pier at Weston-super-Mare continues to rot away in the winter of 2016. This view is looking down from the shore onto the north side of the bridge that links the mainland with Birnbeck Island.
images.alt: The old Birnbeck Pier at Weston-super-Mare continues to rot away in the winter of 2016. This view is looking down from the shore onto the north side of the bridge that links the mainland with Birnbeck Island.

images.filename: 2016 at Birnbeck Pier - looking down the pier.JPG
images.caption: The old Birnbeck Pier at Weston-super-Mare has been disused for many years now. When the decking started to rot away the boards on the left were laid to allow access to the lifeboat station but even the hardy lifeboat crews abandoned the island last year in favour of a portable building at Kinghtstone Harbour. The first span of the North Steamer Pier collapsed during a storm in December 2015.
images.alt: The old Birnbeck Pier at Weston-super-Mare has been disused for many years now. When the decking started to rot away the boards on the left were laid to allow access to the lifeboat station but even the hardy lifeboat crews abandoned the island last year in favour of a portable building at Kinghtstone Harbour. The first span of the North Steamer Pier collapsed during a storm in December 2015.

images.caption: All the buildings on Birnbeck Island at Weston-super-Mare are abandoned now and the first span of the North Steamer Pier collapsed during a storm in December 2015.
images.alt: All the buildings on Birnbeck Island at Weston-super-Mare are abandoned now and the first span of the North Steamer Pier collapsed during a storm in December 2015.
